summary: Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He taught at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and was a guest scholar at Soka University.
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned his Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under MA supervisor Akiko Walley (attested 2014).

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology. He studied at Indiana University and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. 1996) under Victor H. Mair, Ludo Rocher, and Gregory Schopen, later serving as associate professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008).

Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Yale University (1963) and Harvard University (1965, 1972). He held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1972 to 2017.

Daniel Coit Gilman (1831–1908) studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Humboldt University. He served at Yale and UC Berkeley before becoming president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), the Carnegie Institution (~1902–1904), and the American Oriental Society (1893–1906).

Daniel Cozort is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, also studying with Joe B. Wilson and traditional teachers, and taught at Bates College and Dickinson College (~1989–2021).

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as a director of research at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (~1981–2015) and held posts at the University of Lille and University Lille-III (~1993–2015).

Daniel H. H. Ingalls (1916–1999) was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Harvard and under Willard Van Orman Quine, Walter Eugene Clark, and Kalipada Tarkacharya. He served as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard University (~1958–1983; emeritus ~1983–1999).

Daniel John Gogerly (1792–1862) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as chairman of the Wesleyan Methodist Missionary Society (~1838–1862) and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1858–1862).

Daniel L. Overmyer (1935–2021) specialized in sinology and religious studies, studying at the University of Chicago (~1963–1971). He held positions at Oberlin College (~1969–1973) and the University of British Columbia, where he was department head (~1984–1994) and professor.

Daniel M. Stuart is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. Attested in 2017, he served as assistant professor at the University of South Carolina.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his graduate thesis at Florida State University under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Stuart Capper, Jr. is a scholar of religious studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Virginia under Robert Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago with Wendy Doniger on his committee (attested 2000).

Daniel Veidlinger specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999), and held a post at California State University, Chico (attested 2006).

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Virginia. In 2010, he was attested as an instructor at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.
Daniela Berti works in Indology and ethno-anthropology, having earned her Ph.D. from the University of Siena. She was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya in 2004.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies, holding doctorates from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University. In 2020, she was attested as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London.
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Lausanne by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst and also studied under Ganesh Umakant Thite.

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied at Cheeloo University and under Jacques Bacot. From circa 1953 to 1992, he served as professor of Tibetan language and literature at Minzu University of China.

Daud Ali specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago, later holding posts at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 2009) and SOAS University of London (attested 2013).
